As Nvidia's stock price fell to a new 52-week low due to the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Western scholars began buying low prices. Despite a series of downgrades in stock prices, individual investors seem to be betting on a rebound ahead of Nvidia's earnings announcement. The third-quarter earnings, which will be announced on the 17th (local time), are expected to determine the direction of short-term stock prices and the success or failure of investment by Seohak ants.
According to the Korea Securities Depository on the 16th, Nvidia was the top net buyer of domestic retail investors for the past week until the 13th. The net purchase amount was $319.75 million (about 427.4 billion won), and in particular, $254.85 million (about 340.6 billion won) was purchased and paid on the 13th alone when the news of former CEO Hwang's resignation was reported. In other words, about 80% of the weekly net purchases are concentrated in a day.
Choi Hyun-jae, head of Yuanta Securities' research center, said, "NVIDIA's experience of recovering, which plunged after last year's deep shock, seems to have acted as a learning effect, encouraging low-priced purchases."
Nvidia shares continued to weaken due to concerns over slowing data center investment, but news of Hwang's resignation became a catalyst and increased its fall. On the 12th, it fell to $148.80 during the day, setting a new 52-week low. On the 13th, the next day, it closed at $162.85, but it is down 32% compared to the October high of $239.24. As a result, Nvidia's ransom has returned to its level more than a decade ago. According to FactSet, the 12-month forward price/earnings ratio (PER) has recently fallen to about 11.7 times. The figure is below 12 times for the first time since 2012.
The market is paying attention to Nvidia's third-quarter earnings release on the 17th. Experts cited the mass production and delivery schedule of the next-generation chip "Vera Rubin," product transition margin, and whether major customers maintain orders as key points to watch rather than the performance itself.
Lee Kyung-min, a researcher at Daishin Securities, said, "The outcome of this earnings announcement is whether the fourth-quarter guidance exceeds the consensus ($123.3 billion to $124.5 billion) and a 74% defense of gross profit margin."
The possibility of a change in business strategy due to a leadership vacuum is also a variable. This is due to concerns that the large-scale contract that former CEO Hwang himself brought could be shaken. Morgan Stanley said in a report on the 13th, "Jensen Huang's resignation is a big blow considering his performance," adding, "Under the 'temporary' CEO system, it may be more difficult to make promises to customers and create large-scale investments." In addition, it lowered its earnings estimate by 10% next year and lowered its target price from $300 to $267, reflecting Chinese regulatory uncertainty. Some are cautious that even if performance exceeds expectations, it is difficult to expect a rebound in the short term. Choi, director of the center, said, "Even if the performance is good, it is difficult to act as a positive factor, but if it falls below market expectations, it can be a bad news."
